newsitem.title: FRANCE: Barry Callebaut official sees steady cocoa prices.
newsitem.headline: Barry Callebaut official sees steady cocoa prices.

text.p: Rudy Pachl, chief operating officer of Barry Callebaut AG, said on Tuesday he did not expect sharp fluctuations in world cocoa prices in the short term, predicting futures prices may remain at around 1,000 stg per tonne.
The London LIFFE July contract hit a high of 1,065 stg in early April but was trading at 1,021 stg at 1027 GMT on Tuesday.
"I don't think we will see great upwards or downwards fluctuations. I see prices remaining at around 1,000 stg," Pachl told Reuters following a news conference.
Earlier Pachl had said that after a slight deficit between supply and demand this year, the market should be balanced next year due to increased production in some African countries.

"We think that with the results of this year, that is a slight (production) deficit, we should see an equilibrium next year. We think an increase of some three percent in consumption will be followed by an increase in production in some countries such as Ghana and Ivory Coast," he said.

Barry Callebaut data released at the conference showed the company expects the world cocoa bean harvest to decline to 2.698 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 2.852 million tonnes in 1995/96, but to increase in the longer term.
Top producer Ivory Coast is expected to harvest 1.145 million tonnes of beans in 1996/97 against 1.151 million tonnes in the previous season, with higher production forecast for the longer term.
Barry Callebaut also expects world demand for cocoa beans to rise by three percent in 1996/97 to 2.76 million tonnes from 2.679 million in 1995/96.
"We think that that consumption will continue to rise in the long-term," Pachl said.

The Barry Callebaut group, formed by the merger of France's Cacao Barry and Swiss Callebaut ERG, expects to process some 300,000 tonnes of cocoa beans in 1997, reaching a world market share of 12 percent.
